Helps a client or reviewer understand how an authored timber-house assembly relates to a walkable finished space.
Observed mechanism sequence: 01-a-the-board
An annotated component assembly becomes one continuous interior visit through the east threshold, living area and loft.
A future, explicitly authorized component reading could evaluate absolute transforms and matrix-following annotations for only demonstrable groups.
Helps a client or design reviewer understand how the floor, four elevations and ceiling of this authored kitchen relate to the enclosed room and its usable interior.
Observed mechanism sequence: 01-b-unfolded-room
A developed room drawing folds around its real pictured floor, then a camera passes through the same door to inspect kitchen and window bench.
A bounded room-face reading could unfold only validated faces and openings while retaining the real room identity.
Explains the vertical organization and level-three workspace of one authored multilevel timber building to a client or design reviewer.
Observed mechanism sequence: 01-c-floor-by-floor
An exploded building stacks from the ground upward, holds an upper-level gap to reveal the studio, then lowers the overhead plate as the camera traverses that same floor.
Represent real project levels in compact/exploded form with existing Rubik authority and lifecycle.
If a future professional service requires continuing from level reading into a verified room visit, connect only a real selected level/entry/route.
Helps an architect explain how a section drawing relates to occupied rooms, vertical movement and the garden-facing exterior of the same house.
Observed mechanism sequence: 02-demo-section-sweep
A technical section gains depth and material, the viewer follows a continuous route through upper, entrance and garden levels, then returns to the original sheet.
If technical ink is needed, render a section-readable technical view of current Rubik geometry.
If a spatial materialization service is selected, coordinate technical and lit representation over one project.
If a section-to-room visit is selected, continue from a real section to a validated room route.
Helps an architect explain what rooms and vertical movement lie behind one hillside section drawing while keeping the cut readable as perspective, material and light are introduced.
Observed mechanism sequence: 03-a-open-the-lens
One technical 1:100 section opens its lens without losing the cut, gains material and sunlight, visits stair/rooms/pool and returns to a material section before editorial service copy.
Keep a section’s real cut/frame readable while a Story lens opens.
If useful, show the same authorized cut changing from technical ink to lit material without geometry replacement.
If the service is selected, visit meaningful rooms along a real project section and return cleanly.
Helps an architect explain how one hillside house connects its street, bedroom and garden levels through the stair while retaining the section as the common spatial reference.
Observed mechanism sequence: 03-c-down-the-stair
A measured section gains depth and material, the camera descends from street kitchen through bedroom and living levels to the pool, then returns to the whole material section.
Explain street-to-garden circulation on a current Rubik project section.
If useful, carry one real cut from technical ink to lit material during the descent.
Return cleanly from a section story without stale captions or room labels.
Explains a proposed construction sequence for one hillside house through an aligned programme, staged 3D site and fixed-week drawings.
Observed mechanism sequence: 04-demo-build-time-lapse
The visitor sees excavation through structure, props, finishes and handover while a week indicator and programme move together, then the completed house returns to drawing 06 on the six-view sheet.
Present an authorized construction state for actual Rubik elements at a chosen time.
Compare one real Building at several authorized time states.
Keep presentation playback and reverse tied to current project state.
Communicates an example 14-week timber-house construction sequence with an aligned programme and visual build.
Observed mechanism sequence: 05-a-the-programme
A viewer can scrub the same authored week across Gantt rows, staged house pieces and an automatic five-stop handover tour.
Seek and replay a presentation week deterministically.
Show a visual phase of actual Rubik Building elements.
Expose a real planned and actual construction Gantt if product scope calls for it.
Explains how one planned building emerges from a foundation drawing and construction programme on its actual site footprint.
Observed mechanism sequence: 05-b-1-1-site-sheet
A viewer follows the same authored week across printed plan, programme, staged geometry and camera, ending with the complete house over its drawing.
Seek a deterministic visual time state.
Present a project drawing and authorized schedule as one spatial site sheet.
Use factual planned and actual construction dates on a site sheet if product scope later requires it.
Shows an illustrative construction sequence from a site-camera viewpoint while connecting visible build stages to a programme, a changing daylight clock and a final interior walk-through.
Observed mechanism sequence: 05-c-site-camera
A viewer can see how the same timber house rises over 14 authored weeks, approach it after handover and inspect five interior locations.
Seek and restore a presentation time state.
Coordinate a site-facing camera and solar presentation with current Building geometry.
Show factual planned and actual site progress if product scope calls for it.
Lets an architect explain to a client how one physical 1:100 study model relates to the spatial scale and lived rooms of the proposed house.
Observed mechanism sequence: 06-demo-card-model
The same house and contoured site move from card and desk into a materialized exterior/interior visit, reveal a nested model in the study, and return to the original card presentation.
If approved later, present a project-derived physical study model while preserving real project units and geometry.
If useful, show the same authorized building changing representation through a spatially coherent front.
If the professional service is selected, carry the scale explanation through valid project rooms and return to the starting model.
Let an architect or client read one drawn street elevation as a sunlit, materialized house and follow its front door through actual room relationships to the rear courtyard.
Observed mechanism sequence: 07-a-one-door
The same townhouse drawing gains depth, brick and physically related shadow; a reversible camera route tests entry, parlour, atrium and garden continuity.
If selected later, preserve the same project facade while moving from technical shadow hatching to sourced material/light.
If selected later, relate one facade opening to valid room and garden stops while preserving reverse.
Let a developer, architect or buyer compare six distinct townhouse plots in one street composition, identify the available plot 04 and inspect its entrance and key rooms.
Observed mechanism sequence: 07-b-the-row
The same numbered row changes from drawing to materialized street while plot 04 stays identified; the route enters its show house and ends in the atrium facing its garden.
If later selected, show source-backed multi-plot identities/statuses and select one valid project/building for a visit.
If later selected, carry one coherent shadow/ink/material front across an authorized street ensemble.
If later selected, follow the chosen plot from row to valid rooms and return to the original row.
Let an architect, material supplier or client inspect how a proposed facade bond and physically projecting headers read at drawing scale, under normal/raking sun and at human approach scale.
Observed mechanism sequence: 07-c-the-face
A 1:20 ink facade becomes a material wall; the same header lattice casts changing real shadows, is inspected close up and remains continuous through the porch into the hall.
If later selected, tie a material/relief demonstration to verified project/facade dimensions and material identity.
If later selected, show that the same sourced relief produces both technical hatching and physical/raking shadows.

technicalPrerequisites.statement: TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: verified component ownership/membership before transform lease
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: actual navigable threshold/room stops before walk handoff
Technical reuse with FT3D-5 is not product fusion
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: prove room-to-wall-face topology and opening side/owner before any temporary hinge evaluation.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: represent shared, non-rectangular and ceiling-absent cases explicitly or exclude them with a reason.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: obtain a real route/threshold before camera handoff; donor coordinates are not Rubik route authority.
Technical reuse of Story and geometry does not merge Unfolded Room with Board or FT3D-5 as a product service.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: actual Building level descriptor and current geometry for any level reading.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: a valid selected room/entry/route and recomposed camera pose before any automatic visit handoff.
The stretched donor core, fixed six groups and invented construction schedule are reference-only demo content, not product dependencies.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: a supported real Section descriptor/caps and current Building geometry before technical or materialized section output.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: a valid selected room, entry and route before any walkthrough handoff.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: one reversible Story state and Rubik-owned camera/material/light snapshots across any composed transition.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: real Section descriptor/caps and current Building geometry before any section lens or material-front presentation.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: selected room IDs and valid route before section-facing room stops.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story-owned absolute state and restore before any reversible coupled camera/material sequence.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: real Section descriptor/caps and current Building levels before section-facing stops.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: project-derived room/level IDs and route validity before stair descent choreography.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story-owned absolute progress and restore before any coupled camera/material narrative.
PRODUCT_CONTRACT_DECISION: illustration versus real planned/actual construction progress must be explicit before durable schedule data.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: preserve real Project/Building element IDs and their mapping to any authorized jobs before temporal visibility.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story-owned absolute seek and clean restore before multi-view or paper/site presentation.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: isolate render passes and resources if the same Building is shown at several times.
PRODUCT_CONTRACT_DECISION: illustrative construction story versus real editable plan and actual execution.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: explicit Rubik element-to-work membership and date provenance before temporal visibility is treated as factual.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: retain Story-owned seek and lifecycle; do not use C1-C4 quantity tables as job schedules.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: responsive chart and camera layout if a schedule presentation is later authorized.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: authorized plan projection and stable Building element identity for any project-specific on-site sheet.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: validated element-to-task mapping and date provenance before a week is factual.
PRODUCT_CONTRACT_DECISION: illustrative construction story versus real planned/actual execution.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story owns presentation seek and restore; no duplicate timeline authority.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: stable Building IDs and authorized element-to-work membership for project-specific build stages.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story owns camera/light presentation and lifecycle restoration.
PRODUCT_CONTRACT_DECISION: illustrative site story versus factual planned/actual execution.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: date, time and sun labels need explicit provenance before use as professional telemetry.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: current project geometry and authorized site/bounds before deriving any card support.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: one Story-owned absolute state and restore before a reversible representation/light front.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: valid room/entry/route data before a house-scale interior visit.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: authorized facade/opening and valid room/route data before any front-to-back visit.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story-owned absolute presentation state and restoration before reversible ink/material/sun/door coordination.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: material and light authority remains Rubik-owned; any hatch adapter must follow its shadows, not invent project solar facts.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: authoritative plot/building identities and status provenance before any multi-plot claim.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: valid selected-plot opening/room route before a show-house visit.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story-owned reversible material/light/door/camera state before an ink-to-real row transition.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: verified facade bond/projection dimensions and material source before a professional material claim.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: same geometry/normals and Rubik-owned shadow/light authority before comparing technical hatch with raking shadow.
TECHNICAL_PREREQUISITE: Story-owned reversible camera/light/door/material state before a detail-to-interior route.
